title: Spiced split pea pot with marrow and broccoli

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Split peas, tinned tomatoes, spices and fresh vegetables are all ordinary home staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including yellow split peas and marrow in August, is an everyday item at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs one large lidded pan and simple chopping and simmering.

works.reason: 250g split peas in 1.2 litres of water for 45 minutes, then the marrow and broccoli, gives a well-spiced pot for four, with lemon and salt to finish.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for chopping the onion and garlic, peeling and cubing the marrow and cutting the florets, and 8+45+10 minutes matches the 60 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A whole small marrow is a main component of a mild August lunch pot, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pulses with plenty of vegetables make a filling, wholesome family lunch.
